title: LatticeKit: post-quantum cryptography for identity federation
abstractText: Post-quantum cryptography is increasingly deployed in identity federation. Current toolchains suffer from migration of long-lived certificate chains, and closing this gap is still an open problem. In this paper we present LatticeKit, a novel approach that combines policy-as-code with formal verification. The method reduces false-positive rate by 38% and achieves resistance to attacks by cryptographically relevant quantum computers on a public vulnerability corpus. The proposed method is compared against the state of the art on a public vulnerability corpus.

title: On the calibration overhead of surface code
abstractText: Interest in quantum error correction has grown quickly across quantum sensing and adjacent fields. Our approach enables decoders that keep pace with the syndrome stream and reduces qubit overhead by 42% relative to previously reported devices. Experimental results confirm that the proposed method is practical.

title: open-llm: reproducible foundation model baselines and datasets

title: TempoWave: an open evaluation of large language model

Our approach enables stable operation below minus twenty degrees and reduces levelised cost by 18% relative to amine scrubbing. Experimental results confirm that the proposed method is practical.

title: Method for monitoring perovskite tandem solar cell in industrial decarbonisation
abstractText: A pilot plant for perovskite tandem solar cell is disclosed. In known systems, moisture-induced degradation of the perovskite layer is limited by the available cycle life, and reliable operation remains challenging. The disclosed pilot plant comprises a control unit and a techno-economic modelling stage configured to monitor cycle life during operation. The described arrangement enables tandem stacks on existing silicon lines and reduces energy consumption per tonne by up to 46 percent relative to amine scrubbing. Embodiments are described with reference to deployments in the United States.

title: speculative-decoding-kit: reference implementation of speculative decoding for on-device assistants
abstractText: speculative-decoding-kit is an open-source implementation of draft-and-verify decoding for on-device assistants, maintained by contributors from Meta AI Research. The project provides knowledge distillation, reproducible baselines and a test suite covering robustness. However, deployments still suffer from low acceptance rates on long generations; this remains an open problem in low-latency serving. We show that HaloLoop enables lossless acceleration of autoregressive generation and outperforms a tuned dense baseline under low-latency serving. Contributions and issue reports are welcome.

title: Measuring robustness in retrieval-augmented generation deployments
abstractText: Retrieval augmented generation is increasingly deployed in agentic workflows. A key bottleneck is stale documents in the vector index, which existing pipelines do not address. This work presents AuroraMesh, which applies low-rank adaptation to robustness. We show that AuroraMesh enables cheap knowledge updates by reindexing and outperforms the published state of the art under multi-tenant clusters. The proposed method is compared against the state of the art on an internal production trace.

title: FluxSync: revisiting reproducibility for protein language model
abstractText: Protein language model (PLM) promises to change how clinical diagnostics is engineered. However, reproducibility is limited by generalisation to sequences outside the training distribution and remains challenging outside curated benchmarks. This work presents FluxSync, which applies lipid nanoparticle delivery to reproducibility. We show that the design enables design of binders without co-crystal structures, which animal model readouts cannot provide. Experimental results on a public reference dataset support the proposed method.

title: Software bill of materials under legacy protocol stacks: an empirical study
abstractText: Recent work on software bill of materials (SBOM) has renewed interest in operational overhead for critical infrastructure. However, deployments still suffer from incomplete dependency resolution in transitive graphs; this remains an open problem in legacy protocol stacks. We introduce CascadeFlow, a proposed method built on remote attestation. We show that the design enables machine-readable inventories for vulnerability triage, which the incumbent perimeter model cannot provide. Experimental results confirm that the proposed method is practical.
